routing.reason: Input validation and error handling in a ~80-line server plus a three-line front-end catch, with seven testable acceptance criteria and no security-sensitive area.
rulings: Ruling: workflow direct — S ticket, seven testable criteria, one developer can do the API, the page and the tests in one go — cost if wrong: a missed edge case is caught by the single review round, and the default workflow would cost about twice as much

Ruling: no security review step — the change only validates input and stops leaking internal messages; no authentication, permissions, payments, personal data or secrets are involved — cost if wrong: a bypass of validation would only be caught by the code review

Ruling: no PM, PO, architect, UX or SEO — acceptance criteria are already testable and the UI change is only showing an existing error message in the existing #error element — cost if wrong: a design gap on the error display shows up at the visual step
Ruling: no squads — the project declares none — cost if wrong: none
Ruling: budget $0.60 — one task, plan, one review round and the visual step — cost if wrong: the run stops before delivery and the user must raise the budget

task.goal: Fix the title validation and error handling of the tasks API, and show the error on the page. (1) In `src/app.ts` and `src/tasks.ts`: validate `title` in POST /api/tasks (always) and in PATCH /api/tasks/:id (when the body has a `title` key) — a missing, non-string, empty or blank title answers 400 `{"error": "title is required"}`; after trimming, more than 200 characters answers 400 `{"error": "title must be at most 200 characters"}`; titles are saved trimmed; no task is created or changed on failure. Validate before touching the database (for instance a small validation error class thrown by the validator and mapped to its status in the handler). (2) Make `readJson` throw a 400 error `{"error": "invalid JSON body"}` when the body is not valid JSON; also reject a body that parses to something other than an object (null, array, number) with the same message rather than crashing. (3) In `createServer`'s catch, answer 500 `{"error": "internal error"}` for any unexpected error, log the real error on the server with `console.error`, and never send `err.message` to the client; keep the 400s of (1) and (2) answered as such. Keep the 404/405 behaviours. (4) In `public/app.js`, the form's submit handler must catch a failed `api()` call and call the existing `show(err)` so the API's message appears in `#error`; keep the form content when it fails and clear `#error` on success (render already does). (5) Tests in `test/tasks.test.ts`, in the style of the existing ones: POST with `{}`, `{"title":""}`, `{"title":"   "}`, a number title, a null title; a 201-char title (400) and a 200-char title after trimming (201, saved trimmed); a title with surrounding spaces saved trimmed; PATCH with an invalid title (400, task unchanged), PATCH with only `done` still works; invalid JSON body on POST and PATCH (400 `invalid JSON body`); an unexpected error answers 500 `internal error` without the internal message (for instance by forcing a failure in the db or a closed database, and spying on console.error so the test output stays clean); and that no task is created after a 400. Run the project's checks (typecheck and tests) before finishing.

criteria.why: validateTitle rejects missing, empty, blank and non-string titles with 400 'title is required' before createTask; tests check no task is created.
PATCH calls validateTitle when 'title' in body, so a null or invalid title gives 400; tests cover it.
Trimmed length over 200 gives the exact 400 message, and the trimmed title is stored; tests check 201 characters and 200 after trim.
readJson wraps JSON.parse and throws HttpError 400 'invalid JSON body'. It also rejects non-object bodies, which is a reasonable extra.
The catch handler logs with console.error and returns a generic 'internal error'; a test forces a DB failure and checks it.
The submit handler wraps the api call in try/catch and calls show(err). This assumes api() throws with the API error message, which was not visible in the diff.
New tests cover POST and PATCH validation, trimming, length, invalid JSON and the 500 path. There is no UI test.

findings.what: PATCH passes body.done through unvalidated. A non-boolean or object value for done would reach SQLite and give a 500 'internal error' instead of a 400. The ticket does not cover this.
Arrays, null and scalar JSON bodies now return 400 'invalid JSON body'. This goes slightly beyond the ticket, but it is sensible and tested.
The client change in public/app.js (criterion 6) has no test. The 500 test uses a temp file DB and drops the table, which is a bit heavy but works.
HttpError lives in tasks.ts, although it is an HTTP concern. app.ts also imports tasks.ts twice, as a namespace and by name.
Title length is measured in UTF-16 code units, so some emoji count as 2 characters. This is minor.

judge.summary: The diff meets all seven criteria with a small, focused change: a shared validateTitle, an HttpError class, and a central error handler that logs internals and returns only 'internal error'. The tests are thorough, with small gaps in done validation on PATCH and no UI test.
